papers.abstract: This study investigates the discovery potential of a singly produced vector-like top quark ($T$) at a future muon-proton collider with center-of-mass energies of 5.29, 6.48, and 9.16~TeV using a model-independent effective Lagrangian consistent with CKM and electroweak constraints. The $T$ quark predominantly decays into $Wb$, with production cross sections peaking at 9.16~TeV and decreasing above 3~TeV due to parton distribution functions (PDFs) and phase-space suppression. Sensitivity is enhanced through optimized kinematic selections, with the hadronic channel providing higher event rates due to the larger hadronic branching fraction of the $W$ boson, while the leptonic channel offers a cleaner background environment. At an integrated luminosity of 3000~fb$^{-1}$, a 3~TeV $T$ quark can be observed with statistical significances of $21.86\sigma$ and $3.75\sigma$ in the hadronic and leptonic channels, respectively. A machine-learning analysis employing a Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) and a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) is performed at 9.16~TeV for $m_T = 3000$~GeV using $S/B$ and $S/\sqrt{S+B}$ as performance metrics. The MLP consistently outperforms the BDT, achieving a hadronic purity gain of approximately 2.62 while maintaining stable performance across all luminosities. These results demonstrate that a future muon-proton collider can probe vector-like $T$ quark masses up to approximately 3.5~TeV, significantly extending the search for physics beyond the Standard Model.

papers.abstract: Wave propagation in periodically time-dependent media can exhibit driven mode conversion that is absent in static or adiabatic descriptions. We show that coherent axion dark matter provides an intrinsic realization of this dynamics for photons propagating in a magnetic field. The background's periodic birefringence continuously rotates the photon polarization and thereby drives magnetic photon--axion mixing. Using Floquet theory, we derive resonant photon--axion conversion when integer harmonics of the axion oscillation frequency compensate the dispersion mismatch, $\Delta_\gamma-\Delta_a\approx n m_a$ with $n\in\mathbb{Z}$. This resonance enables efficient mixing far from conventional level crossing and is lost when the periodic drive is averaged out of the propagation Hamiltonian. The resulting conversion is bounded and unitary, distinct from parametric instability or axion decay. Our framework describes photon propagation in coherent oscillating axion backgrounds and predicts characteristic polarization signatures, which we illustrate in a blazar environment.

papers.abstract: Within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework, we systematically investigate the subleading-twist (twist-3) generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the proton's valence quarks beyond the Wandzura--Wilczek (WW) approximation. The twist-3 GPDs are not independent; through the equations of motion they decompose into a non-genuine contribution and a genuine twist-3 term. The latter encodes quark--quark--gluon correlations and involves interference between the light-front Fock sectors |qqq> and |qqqg>, which are typically neglected in the WW approximation. Using light-front wave functions obtained from diagonalizing the proton light-front Hamiltonian for its |qqq> and |qqqg> Fock components, we compute these GPDs via their overlap representations. To further explore their physical implications, we also evaluate several twist-3--related quantities, including the quark orbital angular momentum, the total quark spin contribution, and the quark spin--orbit correlation. Our results provide new nonperturbative input on higher-twist dynamics particularly multi-parton interference effects relevant for future measurements at the EicC and the EIC.

papers.abstract: Searches for Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) in the neutrino sector have traditionally focused on non-standard neutrino oscillations induced by LIV in vacuum. In this work, we study anisotropic LIV in matter. First, we review vacuum LIV phenomenology, explaining the energy and direction dependence of sidereal modulations for anisotropic coefficients in the Standard Model Extension. We then demonstrate that for high-energy neutrinos, the interplay between anisotropic LIV operators and the Earth's matter potential produces distinct, observable signatures absent in the vacuum case. We identify a crossover regime where the energy-dependent LIV Hamiltonian becomes comparable to the matter potential, leading to strong interference effects. By analyzing the propagation of neutrinos through a realistic Earth model, we establish three key phenomenological consequences: (1) direction-dependent resonant enhancements of oscillation probabilities, (2) a macroscopic breakdown of neutrino-antineutrino symmetry for CPT-even operators, and (3) a significant increase of the $\nu_\tau$ flux due to LIV-driven injection of high-energy neutrinos into the $\tau$ regeneration cycle. These results highlight that accounting for the interplay between LIV and matter is essential for future LIV searches at large-scale neutrino telescopes.

papers.abstract: The twist-3 transverse spin--dependent nucleon structure function $g_2$ arises in high-energy processes involving a transversely polarized nucleon. Its connection to quark--gluon correlations allows for an interpretation in terms of the average transverse color Lorentz force acting on unpolarized quarks inside a transversely polarized nucleon. In this work, we investigate this force using light-front wave functions obtained by diagonalizing the light-front Hamiltonian with quantum chromodynamics inputs within the Basis Light-front Quantization approach. We evolve our results to a common scale of $5~\mathrm{GeV}^2$ and present the corresponding form factors in momentum space as well as the transverse force components in impact-parameter space. These distributions provide a complementary perspective on the Sivers asymmetry in transversely polarized deep-inelastic scattering. In the forward limit, we extract the twist-3 reduced matrix element $d_2$, and our results are found to be comparable with those from other theoretical calculations and experimental determinations.

papers.abstract: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $\theta$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $\theta=\pi$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $\theta=\pi$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $\theta=\pi$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.

papers.abstract: We study top-antitop pair production in proton-proton collisions within the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT) at dimension six. We focus on the top chromomagnetic operator $C_{tG}$ together with the four-quark operators relevant for unpolarized $t{\bar t}$ production. We analyze the top-quark single-differential transverse-momentum ($p_T$) and rapidity ($y$) distributions and the double-differential distributions in $p_T$ and $y$ ($p_T\times y$) at 13~TeV, and we present projections for 13.6~TeV using the same binning. Our highest-order setup combines next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) Standard Model (SM) predictions with approximate NNLO SM-SMEFT interference corrections. We find that higher-order QCD effects are essential for a stable SMEFT interpretation, yielding substantially more robust bounds and milder parameter degeneracies. The strongest sensitivity is obtained for $C_{tG}$. In the combined highest-order analysis of the 13-TeV results and 13.6-TeV projections, we obtain sensitivity to effective scales up to $3.9~\TeV$. Our results show that higher-order differential top-pair production provides a precise and theoretically controlled probe of the top chromomagnetic interaction.

papers.abstract: The LHC is achieving energies never reached before, opening up possibilities for the discovery of exotic particles in the TeV mass range. Such states include magnetic monopoles, which can explain the electric charge quantisation and restore the symmetry in Maxwell's equations with respect to the magnetic and electric fields. Scenarios proposed to shed light to dark matter and neutrino masses introduce high-electric-charge objects (HECOs). The existence of both classes of particles can be probed in precision measurements in a manner complementary to direct searches. We focus on the contributions of such virtual particles to light-by-light scattering in the context of effective field theories and a Born-Infeld scenario. Specifically, measurements of central exclusive production of photon pairs with proton tagging carried out by the CMS-TOTEM Precision Proton Spectrometer with LHC Run 2 proton-proton collision data are used to constrain magnetic monopole and HECOs. Resummation techniques have been employed to deal with the large HECO-photon coupling. Masses of up to a few tens of TeV have been excluded for monopoles and HECOs of various spins and magnetic and electric charges, respectively.

papers.abstract: The precise determination of the parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the proton is an essential ingredient for LHC analyses, including for those at the upcoming High-Luminosity LHC. So far, PDFs are determined from global fits to binned low-dimensional data obtained from unfolded hard-scattering cross section measurements. In this work we demonstrate for the first time the feasibility of neural simulation-based inference (NSBI) for constraining the proton PDFs using a high-dimensional unbinned data set. Exploiting the full statistical power of unbinned data removes the loss of information inherited by the binning procedure. As a proof-of-concept, we determine the gluon PDF from simulated data of top quark pair production at the LHC with $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. Taking into account both experimental and theoretical systematic uncertainties in the detector-level features, we demonstrate how the NSBI pipeline achieves significant improvements in precision compared to low-dimensional binned analyses. Our results illustrate the potential of unbinned inference to reduce the reliance on coarse approximations of uncertainties and their correlations entering PDF determinations, hence contributing to a new paradigm of unbinned detector-level ML-assisted measurements at the LHC.

papers.abstract: Axionic cosmologies constitute a class of models with phenomenologically rich symmetry breaking in the early universe. In the case where monopoles are present in such a background, the axion profile may be deformed; it is possible to construct a ``monopole bag" state composed of a central monopole within a closed axion domain wall. We consider the gravitational properties of this composite defect, and propose that there exist both a horizonless and a black hole-like static solution for different input parameters. For the latter case, we present our results as a first step towards a new construction of a dyonic regular black hole, given the monopole bag's potential ability to evade the usual singular gravitational collapse and retain a non-trivial axionic profile by the exotic electromagnetic properties of an axionic Chern-Simons term.

papers.abstract: The nature of the vector charmoniumlike states $\psi(4360)$ and $\psi(4660)$ is controversial, and the existence of the $\psi(4660)$ has been questioned: the BESIII measurement of $e^+e^-\to \Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ reveals a nearly flat line shape around 4.66 GeV with a nonzero value at threshold, in contrast to the near-threshold enhancement reported earlier by Belle. We address this puzzle in an S-wave coupled-channel framework for $e^+e^-$ annihilation in $\sqrt{s}\in [4.0,5.0]~\mathrm{GeV}$. The formalism includes the open-charm channels $\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$, $\Xi_c^+\bar{\Xi}_c^-$, $\Xi_c^0\bar{\Xi}_c^0$ (via SU(3) symmetry), the inelastic $\psi(2S)\pi^+\pi^-$ channel mediated by $\sigma(500)$ and $f_0(980)$, and the bare $\psi(4360)$ and $\psi(4660)$ as the 4S and 5S excitations. Short-range contact potentials in the heavy-quark limit are used, and the amplitudes follow from solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation. A combined fit to Belle and BESIII data on $e^+e^-\to \Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ and $e^+e^-\to \psi(2S)\pi^+\pi^-$ yields two poles, at $(4401.93 \pm 16.96i)~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $(4631.39\pm 62.96i)~\mathrm{MeV}$, for the $\psi(4360)$ and $\psi(4660)$. Tracing the pole trajectories as the coupling to the bare states is switched off, we show that both poles originate from the bare $4S$ and $5S$ states strongly renormalized by coupled-channel dynamics. In particular, the $\psi(4660)$ emerges as a broad resonance about 58~MeV above the $\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ threshold; its flat line shape follows from this threshold interplay, providing evidence for its existence. Results are cutoff-robust.

papers.abstract: We present MAPFF1.0_Lambda, the first global analysis at next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD of the collinear unpolarised fragmentation functions of Lambda hyperons. The fit is based on data from single-inclusive electron-positron annihilation, and from both neutral-current and -- for the first time -- charged-current semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering. We have adopted a statistical framework based on Monte Carlo sampling and parametrised fragmentation functions in terms of a neural network. The fragmentation function set comprises a total of seven independent parton flavours, allowing for the first independent determination of valence-quark distributions. Our analysis offers new insights into the hadronisation mechanism of strange baryons and establishes a baseline for future phenomenological and experimental investigations.

papers.abstract: In the Type-I two-Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM), the additional scalars may be light ($\lesssim 100$ GeV) without conflicting with experimental constraints from LHC searches or from flavour observables. So far, the studies of light scalars at the LHC have been limited to exploring non-standard decays of the Standard Model (SM) Higgs boson or via $b\bar b$ associated production followed by leptonic decays of the light scalar. A light scalar in Type-I 2HDM can evade these search strategies due to its potentially tiny coupling to the SM Higgs boson and its suppressed coupling to quarks. In this work, we study the electroweak production of scalar pairs involving the light scalar $h$, the pseudoscalar $A$ and the charged Higgs boson $H^\pm$. The subsequent decays of the heavy scalars into $h$ and an electroweak gauge boson lead to multi-$h$ final states, in which the light scalars are typically boosted owing to the hierarchical scalar spectrum. The decay of the boosted $h$ into $b\bar b$ can be reconstructed within a fat-jet containing a pair of $b$-subjets. We find that tagging such a `boosted double-$b$ fat-jet ($J_{bb}$)' signature in association with a SM gauge boson provides an excellent probe of the Type-I 2HDM for hierarchical scalar spectra. Using multiple light mass $M_h$ benchmarks, we demonstrate that such analysis can explore a large region of the parameter space, with the $2\sigma$ exclusion reach for the heavy scalars extending up to $\sim 560$ GeV ($\sim$ 370 GeV) at the HL-LHC with 3000~\fbi (LHC with 300~\fbi) luminosity for light scalar masses in the range $30$--$70$ GeV. Furthermore, we show that significant sensitivity and even resonance reconstruction can be achieved within a model-independent framework, highlighting the robustness of this search strategy.

papers.abstract: We study the low-scale type-I seesaw with three right-handed neutrinos (i.e. heavy Majorana neutrinos) when the CP-violation arises solely from the low-energy Dirac phase $\delta$ of the Pontecorvo-Maki-Nakagawa-Sakata (PMNS) neutrino mixing matrix and the heavy neutrinos have testable mixings. We derive a CP-conserving and non-real structure of the $3\times 3$ orthogonal matrix entering the Casas-Ibarra parametrisation in terms of two real angles and one single imaginary parameter, ensuring that the only CP-violating phases in the neutrino Yukawa couplings are those of the PMNS matrix. We then focus on the case of CP-violation from $\delta$ alone and discuss the phenomenological implications of this hypothesis. We concentrate on quasi-degenerate heavy Majorana neutrinos with masses within $\sim (0.1-100)\,\text{GeV}$, as relevant for low-scale leptogenesis. Only certain subregions of the full ternary space defined by the ratios $\Theta^2_e:\Theta^2_\mu:\Theta^2_\tau$ - where $\Theta^2_\alpha$ denotes the squared coupling of the heavy neutrinos to leptons of flavour $\alpha = e,\,\mu,\,\tau$ - are compatible with Dirac-phase CP-violation while being testable at collider experiments. Our assumption also implies specific forms of the effective Majorana mass parameter that can be tested at neutrinoless double-beta decay searches. Finally, low-scale leptogenesis under this restriction can reproduce the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) and be tested through the combination of direct heavy neutral lepton searches and neutrino experiments. The BAU vanishes in the exact limit of CP-conserving values of the Dirac phase $\delta = 0,\,\pi,\,2\pi$, but the observed BAU can be reproduced within the testable region even if $\delta$ deviates from these values by a factor as small as $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$, with important implications for ultraviolet completions with approximate CP-symmetry.

papers.abstract:
In this work, we study the single production of a vector-like singlet top partner \( T \) at the 14 TeV HL-LHC in the channel \( pp \to T j \) with \( T \to t Z \), \( t \to b W \to b j j \), and \( Z \to \nu \bar{\nu} \). Signal and background samples are generated with MadGraph5\_aMC@NLO v3.5.11, showered with Pythia 8, and passed through Delphes. The dominant backgrounds are \( t \bar{t} \), \( t Z j \), \( ZZ j j \), and \( W Z j j \) (including charge conjugates). A hadronic pre-selection (\( N_j \geq 3 \), \( N_b \geq 1 \), \( N_\ell = 0 \)) is imposed as trigger, followed by optimized kinematic cuts. We perform multivariate classification with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based on jet-level features. Sensitivities at 3000 fb\(^{-1}\) are quoted using the Asimov significance, \( S / \sqrt{S + B} \), and an Asimov variant with a 20\% background systematic.
  The model parameters \( g^* \) and \( R_L \) are defined in Sec.~2, and a single global working point is used to avoid per-mass tuning bias. In the \( (g^*, m_T) \) scan, we present 2\(\sigma\) exclusion and 5\(\sigma\) discovery contours for \( R_L = 0 \) and \( R_L = 0.5 \). For \( R_L = 0 \), 2\(\sigma\) exclusion corresponds to \( g^* \in [0.17, 0.49] \) (\( 0.16, 0.43 \)) over \( m_T \in [1.8, 2.7] \) TeV, while 5\(\sigma\) discovery corresponds to \( g^* \in [0.27, 0.44] \) (\( 0.26, 0.40 \)) over \( m_T \in [1.8, 2.2] \) TeV for XGBoost and GNN respectively.
  For \( R_L = 0.5 \), the 2\(\sigma\) reach is \( g^* \in [0.21, 0.48] \) (\( 0.20, 0.43 \)) over \( m_T \in [1.8, 2.5] \) TeV, and the 5\(\sigma\) reach is \( g^* \in [0.33, 0.43] \) (\( 0.31, 0.49 \)) over \( m_T \in [1.8, 2.2] \) TeV, with the GNN yielding slightly stronger and smoother limits across the scan.

papers.abstract: The matrix element method (MEM) provides a fully probabilistic approach to confront experimental events with theory, retaining all correlations in the scattering matrix element. While leading-order MEM is widely used and automated, extending it to next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD is challenging due to infrared divergences, negative weights, extra final-state partons, and multi-dimensional phase-space integration. We demonstrate that the POWHEG method offers a practical path to MEM at NLO accuracy. By projecting real-emission events onto Born kinematics via the mappings inherited from the $\tilde{B} (\Phi)$ function, our method consistently includes the hardest QCD radiation while preserving the NLO-accurate normalization. As a proof of concept, we apply the method to fully leptonic $W^+W^-$ production in the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT), considering a CP-even dimension-six triple-gauge-boson operator. At the parton level, the resulting NLO MEM exploits spin and polarization correlations in the final-state lepton kinematics, yielding enhanced discrimination between the SM and BSM hypotheses compared with conventional cut-and-count observables. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of incorporating NLO QCD corrections into the MEM and establish a framework for future applications to a broad range of collider processes.

papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of numerous charmed-strange hadrons lying close to the $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ thresholds, we systematically investigate their mass spectra and electromagnetic characteristics, explicitly incorporating the $S$-$D$ wave mixing and coupled-channel effects. For the mass spectra, we employ the one-boson-exchange model and obtain several promising $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular candidates awaiting future experimental confirmation. The coupled-channel dynamics is found to play an essential role: it not only enhances binding in existing channels but also generates new loosely bound states that are absent in the single-channel approximation. Regarding the electromagnetic characteristics, we discuss the M1 radiative decay widths and magnetic moments of these charmed-strange molecular tetraquarks based on our obtained mass spectra and spatial wave functions within the constituent quark model. Our results demonstrate that the electromagnetic observables serve as valuable discriminants for clarifying the nature of these hadronic molecules. We encourage experimental collaborations to focus on such predicted charmed-strange molecular tetraquark candidates, especially the genuinely exotic $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ states comprising four different flavors with valence quark content $\bar c \bar s u d$.

papers.abstract: The finite width of broad scalar resonances should be taken into account when relating semileptonic $B$-meson transitions to experimentally reconstructable multihadron final states. The quasi-four-body semileptonic decays $\bar B^0\to a_0(1450)^+ (\to\pi \eta)\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ with $\ell=(e,\mu,\tau)$ provide a platform for investigating the scalar $a_0(1450)^+$-resonance as the lowest-Fock-state quark-antiquark component. We calculate the first five odd $\xi$-moments of $a_0(1450)$-resonance twist-2 light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) using QCDSR within the background-field theory, including vacuum condensates up to dimension six. Based on these moments, two twist-2 LCDA schemes are constructed: a light-cone harmonic oscillator model (S1), whose free parameters are fitted to the first five odd moments, and a truncated Gegenbauer expansion (S2) retaining only $a_{1,3}(\mu)$. The $\bar{B}^0 \to a_0(1450)^+$ transition form factors are then calculated using light-cone sum rules. At large recoil region, we present the TFFs with different scheme. The finite-width effect of $a_0(1450)$-resonance is further incorporated through a two-channel Flatt\'e parametrization including the $\pi \eta$ and $K\bar{K}$ channels. The $\pi \eta$ invariant-mass distribution exhibits a pronounced resonance peak around $s\simeq m_{a_0(1450)}^2$. The spectra of the electron and muon channels are nearly identical, while the $\tau$-channel is significantly suppressed because the larger lepton mass reduces the available phase space. After integration over the full quasi-four-body phase space, the branching fractions are given. We expect that these results will provide useful guidance for future experimental and theoretical studies of $\bar B^0\to a_0(1450)^+ (\to\pi \eta)\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ decay and help improve our understanding of the internal structure of $a_0(1450)$.

papers.abstract: We assess the tension between theoretical predictions and the values quoted by the Particle Data Group (PDG) for the partial decay width and branching fraction associated with the radiative charmonium decay $J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c$. A profile scan over the most recent PDG data depending on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c)$ suggests that the correlation between measured branching fractions is compatible with lattice QCD determinations of the partial decay widths $\Gamma(J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c)$ and $\Gamma(\eta_c\to\gamma\gamma)$. We propose a theoretically grounded photon line shape for the radiative decay spectrum and a prescription for the extraction of (product) branching fractions involving the magnetic dipole (M1) transition $J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c$. This approach obviates the need to modify the photon energy spectrum line shape using empirical damping functions, as done in the most recent experimental extractions of $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c)$ from the photon line shape, thereby eliminating an inherent ambiguity in the determination of the derived observables.

papers.abstract: We compute hard-region contributions to the fermion self-energy and the off-shell fermion--photon vertex in massless thermal QED in a covariant \(R_\xi\) gauge. The calculation includes the one-loop next-to-leading-power and two-loop leading-power terms in the expansion in soft external momenta, together with the zero-temperature counterterms required to remove ultraviolet subdivergences. In the real-time formalism, we first derive symmetry constraints on the two-fermion--\(N\)-photon amplitudes, which lead to distinct selection rules in the soft-momentum expansion. The fermion--photon vertex is decomposed into Dirac-vector and axial-vector coefficients. The former satisfies the Ward--Takahashi identity, while the latter is transverse to the photon momentum. These relations are verified at the integrand level. The hard self-energy corrections computed here produce no finite contribution to the fermion damping rate. Our results provide previously unavailable two- and three-point hard-region data for higher-order analyses of fermion mass shifts and inclusive rates, as well as for the construction of a next-to-leading-order fermionic effective action.

papers.abstract: Collider analyses combine rigorous statistical techniques with state-of-the-art Machine Learning models. However, when the latter are used directly to estimate the likelihood function of the background, hard to quantify systematic effects may bias the estimation of the relevant signal parameters. To address this problem, we present the Minimum Resolution Likelihood (MRL) method, which defines a Fiducial Signal Region that effectively turns the systematic effects into statistical uncertainties. We show with examples that the resulting signal strength estimation has a reduced bias. We consider both toy examples and a realistic application based on the HI-SIGMA technique applied to di-Higgs searches.

papers.abstract: We present a study of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) in neutrino oscillations, with primary emphasis on the interplay between CPT-violating and CPT-conserving Standard Model Extension (SME) coefficients. We find that $a_{ee}$ and $a_{\tau\tau}$ dominate among the diagonal LIV coefficients, whereas $a_{e\mu}$ and $a_{e\tau}$ provide the most significant off-diagonal contributions. In contrast, the corresponding $c_{\alpha\beta}$ coefficients have comparatively sub-leading effects. Taking DUNE as a representative long-baseline experiment, we show that the sensitivity to CP violation is modified by LIV in a parameter-specific manner. We find correlations between off-diagonal LIV parameters, and non-trivial dependence on the new phases. In absence of LIV, DUNE is expected to establish CP violation at $5\sigma$ for a limited fraction of $\delta_{CP}$ values. We find that the presence of $a_{ee}$, $a_{\tau\tau}$, $a_{e\mu}$ and $a_{e\tau}$ weakens the CP discovery potential, reducing the achievable significance to below $3\sigma$ over a substantial fraction of $\delta_{\rm CP}$. The independent impact of $c_{\alpha\beta}$ terms also results in suppression, but in combination with $a_{\alpha\beta}$, they introduce degeneracies, complicating the extraction of $\delta_{CP}$. This generally results in a deterioration of CP violation sensitivities below $5\sigma$. These findings emphasize the importance of incorporating LIV effects in precision oscillation studies at upcoming long-baseline experiments.

papers.abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of heavy quark-antiquark pairs off nucleons in the framework of generalized transverse momentum dependent parton distributions (GTMDs) for gluons. The short-distance part of the process is treated at leading order in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics and in first order in a collinear expansion, which allows identification with the description in terms of Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs). For the results for the structure functions in terms of GTMDs and GPDs we consider only unpolarized (spin-averaged) nucleons, but include all possible azimuthal modulations that can arise. The presented results extend known expressions in the literature and are relevant for experimental studies of this exclusive process at the future Electron Ion Collider. Furthermore, we introduce a convenient decomposition of the gluon-gluon correlation matrix in terms of GTMDs, expanded in a Lorentz basis of symmetric traceless tensors obtained from the partonic momentum $k_T$ and the momentum transfer $\Delta_T$. The adopted notation for the GTMDs relates to the nucleon helicity states at the amplitude level, rather than to polarization states of the incoming nucleon or of the gluons, which makes it more transparent which contributions from helicity difference and helicity flip matrix elements can be accessed with unpolarized nucleon beams.

papers.abstract: Heavy quark effective theory (HQET) permits seven $P$-wave states in each of the $\Sigma_c$, $\Xi_c^\prime$, and $\Omega_c$ flavor-sextet sectors, yet the experimentally visible spectra differ strikingly among the three sectors. We show that strong decays, kinematic thresholds, and configuration mixing act as a dynamical filter between the underlying multiplet structure and the observed resonance spectrum. Using QCD sum rules for the masses and light-cone sum rules for the strong decays, we find that only four $\Sigma_c$, four $\Xi_c^\prime$, and five $\Omega_c$ states are sufficiently narrow to contribute to experimentally identifiable resonance structures. The four narrow $\Xi_c$ states, $\Xi_c(2882)$, $\Xi_c(2923)$, $\Xi_c(2939)$, and $\Xi_c(2965)$, and the four narrow $\Omega_c$ states, $\Omega_c(3000)$, $\Omega_c(3050)$, $\Omega_c(3066)$, and $\Omega_c(3090)$, exhibit similar mass-splitting patterns and provide spectroscopic anchors for a common $\lambda$-mode multiplet structure, supporting the successive assignments $J^P=1/2^-,3/2^-,3/2^-$, and $5/2^-$. We tentatively interpret $\Omega_c(3119)$ as a predominantly $\rho$-mode state with $J^P=3/2^-$. With this multiplet structure constrained by the $\Xi_c$ and $\Omega_c$ spectra, we predict four relatively resolvable $P$-wave $\Sigma_c$ states that may overlap within the observed $\Sigma_c(2800)$ and $\Sigma_c(2900)$ structures, providing concrete targets for future amplitude analyses.

papers.abstract: Providing a practical and hadron-level definition of multiple jet flavors has been a long-standing challenge in collider physics. Previous work has introduced a data-driven, operational definition of quark and gluon jets, but no robust generalization beyond two jet categories presently exists. To address this, we introduce a machine-learning framework called "simplex demixing'' to extract $T$ jet flavors (or topics in the statistics literature) from $M$ data samples (or mixtures) with minimal constraints. Intuitively, our procedure identifies the maximally separable categories in the data, translating a multi-category classifier on the $M$ mixtures into a bounded geometric object with $T$ vertices. We first demonstrate our procedure on a toy problem to infer the truth-level fractions of down-quark, up-quark, and gluon jets from synthetic mixtures of the three pure samples. We then propose a tag-and-probe strategy to extract multiple light-flavor categories in a more realistic collider setting involving dijet production. As expected, the identifiability of jet flavors depends on their relative abundance in the samples and the hadron-level information available to the classifier architecture. Our work opens the door to data-driven extractions of multiple jet flavor properties at the Large Hadron Collider.

papers.abstract: We study light quark energy loss in a quark-gluon plasma using the holographic falling-string framework on a machine-learning-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for three flavor configurations: pure glue, two-flavor QCD, and full QCD with strangeness. Stopping distances are computed from null geodesics as functions of reduced temperature $T/T_c$ and baryon chemical potential $\mu$. For $T/T_c>1.03$, the flavor ordering of the integrated stopping distance stabilizes to $N_f=2+1>N_f=2>N_f=0$, corresponding to the quenching hierarchy $N_f=0>N_f=2>N_f=2+1$. This agrees with the flavor ordering obtained from the shooting-string $dE/dx$ when both are expressed in the reduced-temperature framework, providing a cross-check between local and integrated observables within the same holographic background. Near $T/T_c\simeq1$, the behavior is more complex due to the interplay between the $a$ and $b$ terms in $A(z)$ and the different $T_c$ values of the three systems. Finite baryon chemical potential monotonically shortens stopping distances and enhances quenching, with enhanced sensitivity near the QCD critical endpoint, consistent with expectations from RHIC beam energy scan measurements. We discuss the geometric origin of the high-$T/T_c$ flavor ordering and possible extensions to heavy-ion transport simulations.

papers.abstract: We study the signal topologies of Higgs-pair production in the semi-constrained NMSSM at large lambda and low tan(beta) at the HL-LHC (sqrt(s) = 13.6 TeV, L = 3000 fb^-1), using four benchmark points drawn from a parameter scan in which the LHC Higgs-sector constraints were not applied. The benchmarks cover exotic h1h1 -> 4a1 -> 8b (BP1, BP3), boosted h1h1 -> 4a1 -> 8tau (BP2) and SM-like (BP4) final states. Signals are simulated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia 8.316 and Delphes 3, with 10^5 events per benchmark. Background yields are taken from published analyses and serve only as illustrative estimates. In this revised version (v2) we add an a posteriori check with NMSSMTools. All four benchmark points are flagged: BP1-BP3 have BR(h1 -> a1a1) > 99%, in conflict with the limits on undetected Higgs decays and with CMS searches for h -> aa -> 4tau and 4b, and BP4 deviates from the measured b- and tau-couplings by more than 2 sigma. The benchmarks therefore do not represent experimentally allowed parameter points, the signal yields apply to the stated branching fractions only, and the earlier statement of 5 sigma sensitivity is withdrawn. The signal rate scales as BR(h -> aa)^2, so a branching fraction compatible with current limits would reduce the yields by one to two orders of magnitude. The detector-level characterisation of the topologies remains of methodological interest. For BP2 (m_a1 = 8.2 GeV), 82.4% of same-a1 tau pairs satisfy Delta R(tau,tau) < 0.4 owing to the boost gamma ~ 7.5, which motivates dedicated boosted-a1 tagging.

papers.abstract: We derive an analytic resummed description of the missing-mass spectrum in monophoton searches for invisible dark photons at electron--positron colliders. In a dark Abelian Higgs model with a light dark fermion, we construct the spectrum from scalar and fermionic real and virtual contributions without relying on a Monte Carlo shower implementation. Sudakov resummation method is used to deal with the collinear divergence. The analytic expressions make the dependence on the dark charges and the logarithmic structure explicit. A simplified reinterpretation of the BaBar monophoton search, accounting for its finite missing-mass resolution, shows that dark-sector radiation can modify the inferred upper limit on the kinetic-mixing parameter by $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ in the benchmarks considered.

papers.abstract: Higgs pair production provides an important probe of the Higgs self-interaction and the Higgs potential structure. We study the lightest neutral Higgs pair production process $gg \to hh$ via gluon fusion at the 14 TeV LHC, in the $U(1)_X$ supersymmetric standard model. As a $U(1)$ extension of the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM), this model introduces new superfields that bring additional one-loop contributions to the production amplitude. We analyze the parameter dependence of the cross section numerically and present contour distributions in two-dimensional parameter planes. The results indicate that the gauge couplings $g_X$ and $g_{YX}$ are the most sensitive parameters, and the model yields sizable new physics corrections under current experimental constraints. This work helps to understand Higgs physics in the $U(1)_X$SSM and guides new physics searches at the high-luminosity LHC.

papers.abstract: The measured hadron yields in heavy-ion collisions are well described by thermal particle production at temperatures close to the QCD pseudo-critical transition. However, if particles are produced in thermal equilibrium, then the in-medium effects, e.g., broadening of their spectral functions, must be taken into account. In this work, we study for the first time the effect of the thermal broadening of the light vector-meson spectral functions on light hadron production in heavy-ion collisions. We generalize the efficient resonance decay framework FastReso to resonances with finite-width spectral functions. We then compute the pion, kaon and proton spectra from the decays of hadron resonances for in-medium and vacuum spectral functions. We perform a simultaneous blast-wave fit with decay feed-down to measured particle spectra in central Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC. We find an increase in pion spectra at low momenta, from including thermally broadened $\rho$ and $\omega$ mesons. Additional pion yield from finite-resonance widths reduces the commonly observed discrepancy between models and data, but does not completely resolve the soft pion puzzle in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN experiment reported a candidate nuclear recoil at $248\,\mathrm{keV}$. This work proposes that endothermic self-scattering $\chi_1+\chi_1\to\chi_2+\chi_2$ in the Galaxy can produce an excited dark matter population, whose exothermic scattering $\chi_2+\mathrm{Xe}\to\chi_1+\mathrm{Xe}$ in xenon can account for the LZ candidate event. In a benchmark with a light scalar mediator, the conversion cross section is large enough for high-velocity Galactic dark matter particles to generate an excited fraction at the percent level. For dark matter masses near the TeV scale and mass splittings $\delta\gtrsim 500\,\mathrm{keV}$, the xenon recoil spectrum covers the candidate region and can yield an $\mathcal O(1)$ event count. The $\chi_2$ population produced in the Galaxy is colder than a relic population from the early Universe and yields a different nuclear recoil spectrum.

papers.abstract: An inverse seesaw model for neutrino masses and mixing is proposed, based on the spontaneous breaking of a $D_4$ flavor symmetry. The model simultaneously accounts for the neutrino oscillation parameters, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through TeV-scale leptogenesis, and makes predictions for charged-lepton flavor violation (cLFV) that are consistent with present experimental limits. A phenomenological analysis shows that the model is consistent with the observed neutrino oscillation data for both normal and inverted mass orderings. Successful leptogenesis is realized for the lightest pseudo-Dirac pair in the multi-TeV range. papers.abstract: Single inclusive hadron suppression in high-energy heavy-ion collisions provides a sensitive probe of parton energy loss and jet transport coefficient in quark-gluon plasma (QGP). papers.abstract: Evidence for excesses observed at LHC tend to cluster mostly around 95 GeV and 650 GeV. We claim that a consequent interpretation of the 650 GeV and some additional indications calls for a Randall Sundrum sequence of Kaluza Klein graviton resonances. A common prejudice claims that such resonances should be very heavy, out of reach for LHC. We argue that this is no so. Although present LHC searches seem to exclude these particles below 2 TeV, we explain why this 650 GeV resonance could be one of them. We also explain why ongoing analyses ignore this scenario and apply selections which are only valid for scalar resonances. This could also apply to ongoing searches for Higgs pairs where the search for resonances decaying into SM Higgs pairs ignores the KK graviton scenario. We expect that with a correct treatment, one could very significantly increase the detection efficiency for ZZ and hh channels and achieve, with present data, a convincing proof of our expectations. Channels like h(95)h(125) and h(95)h(95) should be added to present selections. Such improvements should allow to reach a discovery. For the ZZ and WW channels, one can use semi-leptonic and purely hadronic final states, to confirm the tower of KK resonances indicated up to 3 TeV.

papers.abstract: As discussed in a number of recent papers, cosmological stasis is a phenomenon wherein the abundances of multiple cosmological energy components with different equations of state remain constant for an extended period despite the expansion of the universe. One of the most intriguing aspects of the stasis phenomenon is that it can give rise to cosmological epochs in which the effective equation-of-state parameter $\langle w \rangle$ for the universe is constant, but differs from the canonical values associated with matter, radiation, vacuum energy, etc. Indeed, during such a stasis epoch, the spatial average of the energy density of the universe evolves in precisely the same manner as it would have evolved if the universe were instead dominated by a perfect fluid with an equation-of-state parameter equal to $\langle w \rangle$. However, as we shall demonstrate, this equivalence is broken at the level of the perturbations of the energy density. To illustrate this point, we consider a stasis epoch involving matter and radiation and demonstrate that within this stasis background the density perturbations associated with a spectator matter component with exceedingly small energy density exhibit a power-law growth that persists across the entire duration of the stasis epoch. This growth can potentially lead to significant enhancements of structure at small scales. Such enhancements are not only interesting in their own right, but may also provide a way of observationally distinguishing between a stasis epoch and an epoch of perfect-fluid domination -- even if the universe has the same equation of state in both cases.

papers.abstract: A thermal plasma dresses soft gauge fields, turning them into collective modes with a plasmon gap and Landau damping. In this paper, we ask whether a thermal radiation plasma does the same to gravitational perturbations. For gravity, the thermal soft scale coincides with the Hubble rate. Any such gap therefore lies at the horizon scale, where the expansion of the background cannot be neglected. We model radiation by a conformal scalar and compute its linear response to metric perturbations directly on a flat FLRW background. We test this response against the diffeomorphism Ward identities. The adiabatic dispersion relation yields a gapped collective mode with $\omega_p^2 = 8\mathcal{H}^2/5$, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the conformal Hubble rate. The imaginary part of its frequency, however, is dominated by the background expansion and does not represent Landau damping. In the radiation background, the tensor modes obey a real-time integro-differential equation that reproduces Weinberg's damping of gravitational waves. The initial-time boundary of the retarded response keeps superhorizon modes frozen until horizon reentry despite the gap. The superhorizon growth found in earlier analyses arises from discarding the memory of the retarded response and from a local-equilibrium state prescription that violates the Ward identities. More generally, the Ward identities forbid any local state response beyond the collisionless kernel.

papers.abstract: Gravitational waves induced by primordial density perturbations provide a powerful probe of the Universe's thermal history, which may include an early matter-dominated (eMD) era predicted by well-motivated particle-physics models. The induced GWs can be significantly enhanced when the Universe undergoes a sudden transition from an eMD era to an era with pressure, such as a radiation or kination era. This enhancement arises from the growth of density perturbations during the eMD era and their rapid oscillations during the era with pressure. This phenomenon is called the poltergeist mechanism. In this review, we explain the essence of the poltergeist mechanism and explore concrete scenarios in which such an enhancement can occur.

papers.abstract: In shift-symmetric Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, stationary black holes have a non-vanishing scalar charge. During the inspiral, the phase evolution is modified by several effects,primarily an additional scalar dipole radiation, which enters at -1PN order. Including corrections up to 2PN, this effect accelerates the inspiral when compared to general relativity, but changes in the conservative dynamics may do the opposite. Using fully non-linear numerical simulations of quasi-circular, comparable mass binaries, we characterize the late stages of the orbital dynamics. We find that the overall effect is still an accelerated merger phase for the modified gravity case, but noticeably less than predicted by PN alone, which we relate to the conservative dynamics, showing that at the late inspiral stage more energy must be emitted in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity to induce a given change in frequency. In longer signals, this may lead to a distinctive frequency evolution relative to general relativity as the binary approaches merger, but its effect close to merger is to suppress the difference with GR. This work suggests we may need to revisit existing constraints on the theory that are obtained assuming PN approximations apply up to merger, or based on order by order approximations that neglect backreaction effects on the metric, and shows the importance of including non-linear effects that modify the gravitational sector in the strong field regime.

papers.abstract: Cosmic birefringence, characterized by the observed rotation of the polarization plane of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation, serves as a critical probe for testing theories beyond the standard cosmological scenario. As a major component of the universe, dark matter plays a pivotal role in cosmic evolution, particularly in the formation of large-scale structures. However, its fundamental nature remains elusive. Axion-like particles (ALPs), as promising dark matter candidates, possess unique advantages in naturally explaining such phenomena. Previous studies on the implications of cosmic birefringence for these ultralight ALP fields have focused on single-field models with conventional potentials. These models face exclusion due to the washout effect - a suppression of the CMB polarization power spectrum induced by oscillatory dynamics of the scalar field within the mass range of less than $10^{-23}$ eV. To address this limitation, we develop a more general theoretical framework incorporating two ALP fields, providing analytical approximations and numerical calculations. Our findings reveal that the superposition of two ALP fields with distinct masses can relax the constraints imposed by the washout effect and reconcile with observations.

papers.abstract: We establish a comprehensive framework for characterizing the infrared (IR) phases of a fermionic quantum theory in three spatial dimensions, based on its quantum anomalies associated with a finite symmetry. We uncover a fundamental dichotomy among these anomalies: the first class of anomalies can always be realized by symmetric gapped states, while the second class can never be realized by gapped states without breaking the given symmetry, establishing the phenomenon of symmetry-enforced gaplessness in these settings. Moreover, using the construction of symmetry extension, we construct the candidate gapped states that theories with the first class of anomalies can flow to in the IR. As an application, we provide concrete predictions of the candidate IR phases of (3+1)-dimensional gauge theories based on our results. Our results also suggest that systems with discrete chiral anomalies cannot be gapped out by adding arbitrary bosonic degrees of freedom.

To further investigate the origin of this excess, we calculate spin-dependent radial disk temperature profiles across all epochs. We show that the soft spectral state of MAXI J1820+070 is well-described by the Comptonized emission from a thin relativistic accretion disk and two blackbody spectral components with kT$_{bb} = 0.5$ keV and kT$_{bb} = 0.2$ keV. Our results indicate that the black hole in MAXI J1820+070 is rapidly spinning, with $a$ > 0.8, potentially powering the relativistic jets. This behavior is consistent with a small disk truncation, a phenomenon recently predicted by GRMHD simulations of the plunging region. The two blackbody components are considerably cooler than the inner disk, corresponding to large emission regions. This suggests that this emission may originate from warm corona layers located further away from the black hole, in close analogy to the warm Comptonization models proposed to explain the soft X-ray excess in active galactic nuclei.

papers.abstract: We present GreyRing, a new model for the post-merger signal in black-hole binary coalescences based on the graybody factor of the remnant. The model accurately reproduces the full frequency-domain ringdown signal of a large set of comparable-mass, aligned-spin numerical relativity waveforms, achieving mismatches of order ${\cal O}(10^{-6})$ for the dominant $(\ell,m)=(2,2)$ mode, and typically outperforming state-of-the-art time-domain models. Building on this model, we introduce a novel consistency test of strong gravity based on the graybody factor: the remnant mass and spin inferred from GreyRing can be compared with those obtained through standard black hole spectroscopy. This agnostic test relies exclusively on the post-merger signal and does not require the inclusion of overtones or the choice of very early ringdown starting times, combining the advantages of inspiral-merger-ringdown consistency tests and traditional black hole spectroscopy. We apply the test to GW250114 and find that the remnant mass and spin inferred from GreyRing are consistent with those measured from the full signal. Remarkably, the inferred parameters can be measured with a precision comparable to, or slightly better than, that achieved with standard black-hole spectroscopy. Our graybody-factor waveform model allows for new precision tests of strong gravity using the ringdown signal.

papers.abstract: We present a density functional-based equation of state for warm, dense nuclear matter with a transition to deconfined quark matter for applications to simulations of supernova explosions and neutron star mergers, but also for the cosmological evolution of Q-balls. For the quark matter equation of state, we employ a recently developed confining density functional approach while nuclear matter is described within a relativistic density functional model of the DD2 class. The phase transition is obtained by a Maxwell construction at constant entropy per baryon. We discuss the solutions of TOV equations for isentropic hybrid stars for two hybrid equation of state models: DDf-SFM without and DD2-$\chi$CDF with color superconductivity. We find that at finite temperatures above a critical value of entropy per baryon sequences of disconnected third family branches ("thermal twin stars") may appear for the DDf-SFM model, while they are absent for the color superconducting model and at $T=0$. We discuss the relation of this critical entropy per baryon to the Seidov criterion of gravitational instability for $T=0$ and find that it is a good guide. An invertible bulk reproduces conventional anomaly inflow; a bulk with non-trivial topological excitations yields a non-invertible generalization. To describe the holographic theory of anomalies, we explain the distinction between uniquely defined topological order and many versions of topological quantum field theory and discuss the boundary-to-bulk map. As an application of the holographic theory of anomalies, we describe morphisms between local quantum theories (such as quantum field theories). These morphisms are built from a bulk domain wall and an invertible boundary junction, which give rise to a sandwich picture. In particular, a fermionic theory can be viewed as a theory with a particular non-invertible gravitational anomaly. Those examples also reveal that {\it symmetry $\sim$ gravitational anomaly $\sim$ topological order in one higher dimension}.

We provide the geometric tools for area metrics that do not rely on perturbation theory and allow a systematic construction and study of general non-linear area metric actions: an algorithm that extracts a length metric from an area metric and a connection on two-forms that is uniquely determined by the area metric, together with its curvature and curvature invariants. Additionally we discuss cosmological backgrounds and the role of the matter coupling, which together open the way to cosmological applications.

papers.abstract: Local out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) measure the growth of initially small commutators. We then prove that, in a Gibbs state with uniform exponential clustering, the full dOTOC obeys the same bound, $D(t) \lesssim t^d$, improving our earlier suboptimal $t^{3d}$ bound. We illustrate these results in two quantum many-body systems: a Brownian coupled-cluster model and a finite-temperature SYK chain. In both cases, an exact disorder symmetry relates $D(t)$ to $\bar C(t)$ and allows us to follow the same extensive observable from the pre-scrambling Lyapunov regime into the post-scrambling growth associated with an expanding saturated region. This late-time power-law growth is the concrete realisation of the weak quantum chaos introduced in our earlier work.

papers.abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

papers.abstract: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.

papers.abstract: Black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. We study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes. Coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed UV dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. For real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. Near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. This mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. Exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. Local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.

Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theoris, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. papers.abstract: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+\omega$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.

papers.abstract: The Brout--Englert--Higgs (BEH) mechanism can be formulated in gauge-invariant relational terms without assigning physical spontaneous breaking to a local gauge redundancy. We treat the gauge orientation of the Higgs field as dynamical internal reference data and describe the gauge connection relative to this Higgs frame. On a regular patch where the frame exists, the Higgs kinetic term induces a positive-semidefinite mass-squared quadratic form on the gauge-orbit directions and reproduces the standard tree-level vector masses. A complete Higgs frame yields a gauge-invariant relational connection, whereas a partial frame is defined only up to a stabilizer group $H$ and produces Higgs stiffness only along the coset directions $G/H$. In quantum field theory the normalized frame and relational connection are nonpolynomial composite variables; physical masses are therefore characterized through suitably renormalized gauge-invariant composite correlators, or through fully dressed operators in residual-charged sectors. Applying this construction to the electroweak theory, we show that the Higgs frame relationalizes the $SU(2)_L$ redundancy while leaving a residual electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm em}$ Gauss law: $W^\pm$ and charged fermionic modes require electromagnetic dressing, whereas neutral channels admit local gauge-invariant interpolators. This formulation connects Higgs dressings, FMS composites, and internal quantum-reference-frame language while keeping local mass generation distinct from global symmetry realization and topological obstructions.

We demonstrate that these higher-order corrections become dynamically significant in the high-energy regime of cosmic inflation, naturally modifying the slow-roll dynamics without requiring a fundamental inflaton potential. A comprehensive phase-space analysis reveals that the quantum corrections drive early-time de Sitter-like attractors, providing a robust mechanism for sustained inflationary expansion. Confronting the model with the Swampland program, we show that the correction factor $\mathcal{F}(H)$ modifies the effective slow-roll parameters, enabling the model to satisfy the Swampland de Sitter and Distance conjectures during the inflationary epoch. We calculate the inflationary observables, including the spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, and demonstrate that the model's predictions are in excellent agreement with the Planck 2018 observational constraints. Our results suggest that thermodynamic duality-induced horizon corrections offer a viable and testable pathway for realizing successful inflation within a well-motivated quantum-gravitational framework.

papers.abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.

papers.abstract: The energy densities of the quantised scalar and electromagnetic fields need not be positive, but their averages along timelike worldlines are constrained by Quantum Energy Inequalities (QEIs) that hold in flat and curved spacetimes for arbitrary Hadamard quantum field states. However the general QEI bound is not easy to compute in closed form. Here, we compute closed form expressions for the massless scalar and electromagnetic fields along stationary worldlines in Minkowski spacetime. These worldlines are solutions to the four-dimensional Frenet-Serret equations with constant curvature invariants and include inertial, uniformly linearly accelerated, and uniformly rotating worldlines as special cases. The QEI bound depends on a choice of tetrad along the worldline, and we compute it for any tetrad with constant angular velocity relative to the Frenet-Serret tetrad. Optimising over the angular velocity, we show that the tightest electromagnetic QEI bound occurs when the tetrad is invariant under Fermi-Walker tetrads. Surprisingly, the Fermi-Walker tetrad does not produce the tightest QEI bound for massless scalar fields, and we investigate the optimal bound both analytically and numerically. Our results and methodology significantly improve on those in [CJ Fewster & J Thompson, Class. Quantum Grav. 40 (2023) 175008], in which only Frenet-Serret tetrads were considered for massless scalar fields.

papers.abstract: Low-energy electrons in graphene obey an emergent, rotationally invariant Dirac equation, while the honeycomb lattice enters only through higher-order, symmetry-breaking corrections, the leading one being trigonal warping. This provides a unique solid-state arena to address a cornerstone challenge in quantum gravity: how to detect ultraviolet symmetry-breaking granular corrections, suppressed by a fundamental scale, atop an emergent infrared relativistic continuum. We show that intense counter-rotating $\omega$-$2\omega$ fields and valley-resolved high-harmonic generation (HHG) provide such a probe. Within a family of models that interpolates continuously between the isotropic Dirac cone and nearest-neighbour graphene at fixed Fermi velocity, the valley contrast of the harmonic yield vanishes identically in the symmetric theory, grows linearly with the warping coupling, and its valley-even counterpart appears only at second order, as expected from effective-field-theory power counting. The stronger the laser, the farther it drives electrons from the Dirac points, so the laser intensity plays the role of the collision energy. For the fourth harmonic, the leading warping correction alone accounts for the valley contrast of real graphene up to fundamental intensities of about $10^{11}$ W/cm$^2$, below the damage threshold of monolayer graphene, whereas the fifth harmonic already reveals higher-order lattice corrections at intensities around $10^{10}$ W/cm$^2$. The two harmonics, which rotate in opposite directions, are emitted by opposite valleys. Valley-resolved harmonics are far more sensitive than the residual valley populations, making them a practical detector of lattice-scale physics hidden beneath an emergent Dirac theory.

papers.abstract: We study dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in $(2{+}1)$-dimensional QED on a rigidly rotating disc, $\Omega R<1$, within the rainbow Schwinger--Dyson framework. At zero temperature the rotation response of the condensate vanishes identically, so $N_c^{\rm SD}(\Omega,T{=}0)=N_c^{\rm SD}(0)=2.60\pm0.01$ (using three operational definitions). At finite temperature, rotation suppresses the condensate through a dominant occupation-reweighting channel, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm occ}=-1.55$, accounting for $\ge 99.995\%$ of the linearized total response at the reference parameters, with self-consistent feedback amplifying it by $26.5$. The screening channel is reported at fixed regularization, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm scr}(\varepsilon = 0.01)=-0.97$; its $\varepsilon \to 0$ behavior is logarithmically divergent. The crossover flavor $N^{*}(\Omega)$ falls monotonically at fixed temperature (a corollary). The critical flavor number is unchanged by rotation at $T=0$ (theorem). Together these results set the finite-temperature reference for the model.

papers.abstract: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.

papers.abstract: We study the conformal coupling in the torsion-free Palatini formulation with an ordinary scalar kinetic term. Tuning the curvature coupling cannot restore Weyl invariance in a Palatini theory with an ordinary scalar kinetic term because, for an independent and inert connection, the scalar-curvature term is separately Weyl-invariant, and no finite curvature coupling cancels the Weyl variation of the kinetic term. This can be demonstrated by evaluating the energy-momentum trace on the scalar equation of motion and noting that it is explicitly independent of the Palatini coupling. Eliminating the connection, we construct a map between the curvature coupling and the effective coupling for the equivalent metric theory, and demonstrate that the scalar continues to propagate even if the reduced kinetic coefficient vanishes. We also show that it becomes a Weyl compensator with a scale-invariant potential only in the rescaled infinite-coupling limit, which in four dimensions is directly related to Palatini ${\cal R}^2$ gravity. We calculate the running of the couplings at one loop, and we find that the conformal shift in the metric-curvature coupling's beta function generates a metric-curvature coupling on a fixed metric-affine background, whereas the independent-curvature coupling runs homogeneously. Furthermore, we follow an alternate prescription in which the connection is allowed to respond to the scalar fluctuations, which results in a different scalar Hessian and therefore different beta functions. Nonetheless, we find that both prescriptions admit the formal infrared limit $(\xi_{eff},\lambda_{eff})\to(1/6,0)$ through different limits of the original couplings in the case of positive perturbative quartics. Finally, we note that trajectories starting on the positive gravitational branch encounter a vanishing gravitational coefficient at a finite scale before this endpoint.

papers.abstract: Tidal Love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. While the static Love numbers of Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic Kerr--Newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. Exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative Love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. We also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.

papers.abstract: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.

papers.abstract: Modifications of gravity beyond (vacuum) General Relativity have a subtle impact on the physics around black holes. Describing these effects across different observables is, however, a priori strongly model dependent. While effective descriptions of the geometry allow to efficiently capture deviations from benchmark predictions, they sometimes lack a clear passage towards (effective) new physics. Inspired by linear response theory, in this work I therefore propose a formalism that allows to calculate leading corrections of observables relative to the Schwarzschild black hole anywhere in space-time (outside of the horizon): the order of corrections is fixed through an eigenvalue $\mathcal{E}$ of the Einstein tensor, which is identified with an external energy momentum tensor that generates the deformation of the geometry. In this ways, $\mathcal{E}$ can be linked to effective physics models. Focusing on spherically symmetric and static black holes, I illustrate the approach at the hand of a number of observables in the vicinity of the horizon, such as characteristic quantities of particles moving around the black hole (e.g. the black hole shadow or the radius of the innermost stable circular orbit) or the spectrum of scalar quasi-normal modes. Reversing the logic, I argue that the knowledge of such observables provides non-trivial constraints on $\mathcal{E}$, which in turn grant insights into the effective physics in the vicinity of the black hole.

papers.abstract: We study collective charge excitations in pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals within the random-phase approximation, considering both the linearised model with a flat-band and its quadratic-corrected counterpart. We analyse their density response, Drude weights, screening, plasmon dispersion and damping, particle-hole continua, and Friedel oscillations from the long-wavelength to the arbitrary-momentum regime. The quadratic correction renders the flat-band dispersive and endows it with a Fermi surface, thereby affecting the overall response. Comparisons with Weyl and Hopf semimetals reveal how bandstructure and quantum geometry jointly govern collective charge dynamics. While the Drude weights are determined by the Fermi surface and band-velocities, interband screening, plasmon dispersion, and Friedel oscillations reflect the quantum geometry of the eigenstates.

papers.abstract: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.

papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.
